title: Harry James and the Goodman trumpeters
summary: James and the Goodman section visited the Ubangi Club; James recorded Hawkins's tune.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I met Harry James when he was with Goodman. I'm downtown at the Harlem Opera House at 52nd and Broadway. I was there for a year. Well, Harry James with Goodman, Harry James and Angels Sing - Chris Griffin and ^ what was his name?
Ziggy Elman. That was Goodman's trumpet section.
Now, they finished. They were at the Pennsylvania Hotel, I believe. I get through at 4. They used to come by the Ubangi Club and sit there, and, you know, listen to me

play. And, that's how we happened to start knowing each other then. And then, I was at the Loew's State. When I looked down there, on the second or third row. There they are sitting, all three of them.

Now, I'm going to Texas to play a one night stand. Harry James' parents live, not Fort WORTH. Some other part of Texas, Port Arthur, Texas. Now, he wrote his parents and told them that I was, I told him that I was going there. He had his parents to come out, and they had a nice table there in front to see me play. I met his parents and everything through that.

Harry James and I, we was pretty close. And when he went to California with his band, he recorded one of my recordings. He said "I'm gonna make 'Don't Cry Baby' you did." You know? I said, that's beautiful. But, we was pretty close. All through this time we had fun.
